title: Ten Days, Measured
summary: Your round-1 red plane and 'Initiate the / System Audit.' kept as you picked them, with the button and the ten working days pulled apart: the decision (lede, paper button, contact link) at left, and to its right, one step quieter, a paper ruler of ten ticks (one per working day) over three plain terms.

reference.site: Round 1 · A ('The Core, Installed') + B ('The Red Field') calm; MEASURE ruler from the A×C system
reference.borrowed: From A (after Studio Freight's contact poster): the flat full-red plane, the paper-square caps label, the flush-left two-voice statement with nothing above it, the paper rule, the lede 'One diagnostic maps the architecture underneath your pipeline. What we build, you keep.', the paper primary with red text and the 'Deployment window open' note. From B (after Legora's closing panel, refs/cta-B.webp): the calm. One statement, two doors, three terms at the right, and a lot of deliberate empty red.
reference.kelwin: A's core plate is gone. It was the logo's small square, and it merged the button with the '10'. The act now has two parts in a fixed order. (1) THE DECISION, cols 1–6: the kit's head grammar on red at 112px, then the lede, then REQUEST A SYSTEM AUDIT ↗ (paper fill, red text) and TALK TO THE TEAM → in the doors position, on their own. (2) THE FACT, cols 9–12, quieter: '■ Deployment window open', then '10 working days' at 32px wide (10 in 430, 'working days' in light 300), then the MEASURE primitive as paper lines on red: a 421px baseline with ten ticks, one per working day, majors at 01 · 05 · 10, labelled '01 Kickoff' and 'Readout 10'. Under it, three static terms in the kit's spec sheet (the same one the interior header uses for its facts): Scope · Three layers, fixed up front / Your time · Two sessions, no homework / Readout · Yours to keep, either way. All copy is the live site's audit copy (AuditSpec, FinalCTA). The terms are deliberately NOT an accordion: the FAQ directly above is a +/− ledger beside a head and button, and repeating it here made the close read as a second FAQ and gave the reader a control competing with the button. Alignments: the column's label square sits on the rule's centre line, so both halves start on one horizontal; '10 working days' shares the lede's first baseline; the terms' first hairline sits on the button's bottom edge; every term value starts on col 10. Red: the plane itself. Every accent inverts to paper, and there is no other red.

motion: entrance (the kit's head, 0–1.3s): the label row fades in. 'Initiate the' rises out of its mask, and the light 'System Audit.' follows 200ms behind. The paper rule draws at 520ms, the lede fades up at 600ms and the two doors at 700ms. The decision is complete before the fact begins.

the one orchestrated moment (MEASURE, 0.8–2.9s, travels the fact column top to bottom): '■ Deployment window open' fades in and '10 working days' rises 12px. The ruler's baseline draws left to right (700ms). The ten ticks drop in one by one at uneven spacing (40ms stagger, 320ms each), and the fixed ends, '01 Kickoff' and 'Readout 10', fade in. At 1.7s the ticks SETTLE: the eight inner days slide into an even calendar (1.2s --ease-inout) while both ends hold. In step, the numeral counts 00 → 10 (1.5s, JS; its box is held at the final width, so 'working days' never moves).
then the three terms rise into place, 80ms apart (2.4–3.2s). Nothing opens and nothing loops: the plane is at rest by about 3.2s, leaving the button as the only thing to act on.
interaction: kit hovers only. The paper button goes to blush with ↗ moving 2px up-right; the contact underline turns paper and → moves 3px. The terms are static text, by design.

on the live site: the head and the ruler play once when the plane is 40% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin). With reduced motion, KM.init({reduced:true}) returns at once: even ticks, '10', all terms visible, no timers.
notes: Stage ≈957px: 160 + label row + 112px two-line statement (held at 227px so every line below lands on whole pixels) + the act + 160. Fact column = cols 9–12 (x 954.7 → 1376, 421px), placed in the head grid's rows 3–6; row 6 is 1fr, so the column's height never pushes the doors away from the lede. The ruler is one inline SVG, 1px crisp strokes in --fg with a --line-2 baseline: 8px day ticks, the 05 major 14px, the ends 20px (the hero's band ruler uses the same grammar, so the page opens and closes on one measure). The numeral uses proportional figures because Mona's tabular zero is slashed. The terms use the kit's .ac-spec (mono key, Mona 15px value), key column exactly one grid column wide. C quotas: one drawing, no callouts, no dimension lines, no registration marks, no title block; mono limited to 'Fig. 12', the ruler values and the three term keys. Review pass (round 2): replaced the opening +/− terms ledger with static terms, because it repeated the FAQ immediately above (same head-left / ledger-right composition, same toggles, same open row) and added a second control to a conversion plane; the JS is now only the day count. Both skins checked.
addressed: The button and the '10 working days' are now two separate things. The decision (the line under the headline, Request a System Audit, Talk to the team) sits at left on its own; the ten days have their own quieter column at right.

Clear order: headline first, then the paper button (the only solid object on the red), then the ten days and the terms in thin lines and light type, so they inform the decision without competing with it.

The logo-symbol 'core' square is gone, and nothing on the plane is built from the logo's corners. The ten days are drawn instead as a ruler: ten paper ticks on the red, one per working day, from Kickoff to Readout.

B's calm: one headline, two doors, three short terms (Scope, Your time, Readout) and a lot of open red. The terms are plain text rather than an open-and-close list, so this section no longer looks like a second FAQ right after the FAQ.
One quiet motion: the ticks arrive unevenly and settle into an even ten-day calendar while the number counts up to 10, then the terms rise into place and everything stops. Nothing loops.
